title: Market signal decomposition and enterprise buyer-fit matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: Build a repeatable framework that decomposes observed market signals (model feature launches, latency/cost claims, licensing shifts, regional availability) into actionable buyer-fit scores and a procurement decision tree tailored to enterprise segments. Deliver a lightweight matrix that PMs and sales can use to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments based on latency/cost/regulatory trade-offs.
background: We frequently receive fragmentation in competitor claims (e.g., sub-20ms token latency vs different prompt lengths, or low-cost quantized variants with unclear quality tradeoffs). Sales and Solutions Engineering need a deterministic way to map those external signals to impact on our buyers (finance, healthcare, platform teams). Current ad-hoc notes delay procurement conversations and lead to inconsistent guidance across account teams.
goals: Create a signal taxonomy that separates: performance claims, availability constraints, licensing changes, and hidden cost signals (e.g., memory-led batch limits)
Produce a buyer-fit matrix scoring model variants across: latency-tolerance, session-size, SLO-criticality, compliance requirements, and cost-sensitivity
Deliver a procurement decision tree with clear triggers for recommending Hosted, Dedicated, or Private
Run empirical probes for 6 representative workloads and publish a companion datasheet with measured P50/P95 latency, throughput, and per-token cost estimates
deliverables: Signal taxonomy doc (Confluence) with examples and ingestion checklist
Buyer-fit matrix spreadsheet (Drive) and a one-page slide for GTM
Procurement decision tree (flowchart) embedded in Console enablement
Empirical probe report (CSV + dashboard link) for 6 workloads
Guidance snippets for Solutions Engineers and Sales playbook
acceptance_criteria: Confluence signal taxonomy reviewed + approved by Research and Solutions Engineering
Buyer-fit matrix validated against 3 enterprise customer accounts and updated with feedback
Probe report shows reproducible latency/cost numbers across 3 infra regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1)
Procurement tree documented with at least two real-case examples and an owner for future maintenance
approach: Phase 1: Signal harvest and taxonomy (2 weeks) - collect competitor releases, public benchmarks, and partner notes. Phase 2: Buyer interviews and matrix prototyping (1 week) - 3 enterprise customers + SE interviews. Phase 3: Empirical probes (2 weeks) - synthetic and replay workloads executed on sample model variants and infra regions. Phase 4: Synthesize into decision tree, GTM slide, and console snippet (1 week).
probe_workloads: Customer service summarization (avg prompt 1k tokens, session multi-turn)
Search reranking embeddings pipeline (100 queries batch)
RAG long-context ingestion + 3x retrievals (10k context window)
Real-time chat frontend simulation (concurrency 50, seq len 512)
risks: Competitor public claims are inconsistent and sometimes optimistically biased
Measured probes may not exactly match customer production workloads -> results must be framed as directional
Cross-region infra variability could inflate cost estimates if not normalized
Stakeholder time (SEs, customers) may delay buyer validation step
